comment: The competitor matrix as the gate sees it: every cell, its state, and the MISSING count.
**MISSING may fall and may not rise.** A cell is measured only when its artifact carries a value produced with the
component the cell names switched on.

measured.name: review.f1.martian
measured.axis: review F1 on the field's corpus

measured.name: retrieval.lexical.recall
measured.axis: lexical search recall

measured.name: retrieval.docstring.recall.withVectors
measured.axis: docstring search recall with vectors registered, at the product default weight

measured.name: retrieval.paraphrase.recall.withVectors
measured.axis: paraphrase search recall at 20 with vectors registered, at the product default weight

measured.name: retrieval.cosqa.mrrAt10
measured.axis: code search MRR@10 on CoSQA, the corpus the field reports on

measured.name: indexing.secondsPerMillionLines
measured.axis: indexing seconds per million lines

measured.name: tokens.reduction
measured.axis: token reduction versus a full-context baseline

measured.name: quality.languageCoverage
measured.axis: providers whose output has been scored

measured.name: review.f1.martian.ourRow
measured.axis: our review F1 under the field harness and its own judge

measured.name: review.f1.aacr
measured.axis: our review F1 on a competitor's published corpus

measured.name: review.findingsPerFile.ocrOnOurCorpus
measured.axis: a competitor's findings per file on this repository's corpus, run by us

measured.name: review.findingsPerFile.sameDenominator
measured.axis: our engine and a competitor over one directory, same mode, same model

measured.name: review.f1.aacr.headToHead
measured.axis: our engine and a competitor on one corpus, one judge, one ground truth

measured.name: crossRepo.importRecall
measured.axis: of the (importing file, imported file) pairs another repository really imports, how many the graph resolved

measured.name: crossRepo.precision
measured.axis: share of resolved cross-repository import edges the independent parser also reports

measured.name: crossRepo.traceRecall
measured.axis: "who uses this symbol in my other repository" answered for every importer the parser names

measured.name: crossRepo.impactRecall
measured.axis: "what breaks in my other repository if this module changes" naming every affected file

measured.name: security.owasp.tpr
measured.axis: OWASP Benchmark true positive rate

measured.name: security.owasp.fpr
measured.axis: OWASP Benchmark false positive rate

measured.name: security.owasp.score
measured.axis: OWASP Benchmark score (TPR - FPR)

measured.name: security.owasp.taintSubsetScore
measured.axis: OWASP Benchmark score over the seven flow categories

measured.name: security.owasp.ruleScore
measured.axis: OWASP Benchmark score of the rule family alone, over all 11 categories

measured.name: security.owasp.flowScore
measured.axis: OWASP Benchmark score of the flow analysis alone, over all 11 categories

missing.name: review.findingsPerKLine
missing.axis: findings per 1,000 lines on the field's repositories

missing.name: qa.accuracy.longCodeArena
missing.axis: recall@10 of the files that must change, on Long Code Arena's bug-localisation test split

missing.name: review.f1.martian.fieldComparison
missing.why: the job scores the whole field with one judge; no artifact yet

missing.name: qa.accuracy.crossCodeEval
missing.why: the dataset (AWS/crosscode-eval) is gated on the hub: an unauthenticated request answers 401, and accepting its licence is a step a CI job cannot take on the maintainer's behalf. Long Code Arena covers the same axis on a corpus that can be downloaded, so the gap is recorded rather than filled with a proxy

missing.name: sast.precision.primevul
missing.why: PrimeVul (Ding et al., 2024) is function-level C/C++ with a JSONL schema of its own; the OWASP figure is a flow-and-rule measurement on Java, so quoting it here would answer a different question than the one this cell asks
